stories.title: Persistent HPV infections linked to cervical precancer risk
stories.summary: New research published in Cancer suggests that increasing and persistently high viral loads in women with HPV infections may indicate the presence of cervical cancer. The study highlights the potential diagnostic value of monitoring viral trends in patients with persistent infections.

stories.title: Wolbachia-carrying mosquitoes reduce dengue and chikungunya in Brazil
stories.summary: A study of 5,700 children found a 69 percent reduction in dengue and chikungunya infections in neighbourhoods populated by mosquitoes bred to carry Wolbachia bacteria. The findings suggest a potential alternative to relying solely on pesticides to control the spread of these viruses.

stories.title: Experimental drug ERAS-0015 shows early promise in cancer trials
stories.summary: Erasca reported that its experimental pill, ERAS-0015, reduced tumours in 44 percent of pancreatic cancer patients and 69 percent of those with specific genetic variations in an early-stage trial. The company describes the results as a major breakthrough for patients with advanced pancreatic and lung cancers.

stories.title: Phase 1 trial reports safety for CD123 CAR T cell therapy
stories.summary: A phase 1 clinical trial at City of Hope evaluated CD123-directed CAR T-cell therapy in patients with relapsed or refractory acute myeloid leukemia. Researchers reported a manageable safety profile with no dose-limiting toxicities, even among patients who had previously undergone allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.

stories.title: Pan-RAS molecular glue shows efficacy in early cancer trial
stories.summary: Results from the AURORAS-1 Phase I clinical trial indicate that the anticancer drug ERAS-0015 is safe and effective at shrinking tumours in patients with lung and pancreatic cancers. The drug is described as a pan-RAS molecular glue.

stories.title: Daraxonrasib and chemotherapy combination shows tumor reduction
stories.summary: A phase 1/2 trial presented at the EORTC-NCI-AACR Symposium found that combining the oral medication daraxonrasib with standard chemotherapy stopped cancer growth in 90.2 percent of patients with advanced pancreatic cancer. Tumours disappeared entirely in 8.2 percent of the 61 participants.

stories.title: Azacitidine mechanism of action re-evaluated
stories.summary: Azacitidine has been used for over two decades to treat blood cancers like MDS and AML. While the drug was traditionally thought to function by stripping chemical tags from DNA to reactivate silenced genes, new research suggests it acts primarily on RNA.

stories.title: Metastatic pancreatic cancer responds to daraxonrasib combination
stories.summary: New results from a Phase I/II clinical trial indicate that the combination of daraxonrasib and chemotherapy caused substantial tumour shrinkage in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer. The findings were shared following recent clinical testing.

stories.title: Daraxonrasib shows potential in advanced pancreatic cancer treatment
stories.summary: A clinical trial suggests that combining the daily pill daraxonrasib with chemotherapy can wipe out advanced pancreatic cancer in one in 12 patients. The lead researcher described the results as the closest thing to a cure for some, noting improved survival rates and fewer side effects.

stories.title: ICMR report confirms rising antibiotic resistance in India
stories.summary: An ICMR report analysing over 113,000 samples from 30 tertiary-care hospitals in 2025 shows that common antibiotics are losing effectiveness. The data suggests that the practice of using partial courses of medication is contributing to the survival and multiplication of hardy, resistant bacteria.

stories.title: Odisha reports 25 lakh patients treated under Ayushman Bharat
stories.summary: Health Minister Mukesh Mahaling informed the Odisha Legislative Assembly that over 25 lakh patients received treatment under the Ayushman Bharat scheme between April 2025 and November 2026. The state expenditure for these services totalled 6,877 crore rupees over the two-and-a-half-year period.

stories.title: ICMR finds common antibiotics losing potency
stories.summary: A new ICMR report indicates that antibiotics are increasingly ineffective against common bacterial infections. Testing revealed that only 18.4 percent of E. coli samples in hospitals remained susceptible to cefotaxime. The health ministry has cited concerns regarding inappropriate prescribing and the sale of antibiotics without prescriptions.

stories.title: India reports decline in tuberculosis burden
stories.summary: India's TB incidence rate fell from 237 cases per lakh in 2015 to 187 in 2024, with mortality dropping from 28 to 21 deaths per lakh. Despite these improvements, the figures remain above national elimination targets. Testing volumes have increased to 2.8 crore in 2025.

stories.title: Health Ministry Proposes Amendment to Drug Rules to Bring Antimicrobials Under Central Regulatory Oversight - DD News
Government reports expansion of Ayushman Bharat scheme
stories.summary: The government states that the Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana now processes over 40,000 claims daily. Since its 2018 launch, the scheme has provided health insurance coverage to families from the poorest 40 percent of society and senior citizens aged 70 and above.

stories.title: Health ministry reports 10 million HPV vaccine doses administered
stories.summary: The health ministry reports that India has administered 10 million doses of the HPV vaccine, reaching 87 percent of its target population of girls within nine months. The initiative is part of ongoing national health programmes focused on infectious disease prevention.

stories.title: India contributes to global decline in child mortality
stories.summary: A 2025 United Nations report highlights India's role in reducing child mortality, noting a 76 percent decline in under-five deaths in Southern Asia since 1990. The report credits targeted public health interventions and improved institutional care for the sustained progress in neonatal survival outcomes.

stories.title: India marks progress in national immunisation coverage
stories.summary: India has eradicated smallpox, polio, and maternal and neonatal tetanus through sustained vaccination efforts. Marking National Vaccination Day, officials highlighted the role of these programmes in strengthening the national healthcare system and protecting millions of citizens from preventable diseases.

stories.title: The United States Has Lost Its Measles Elimination Status - The Scientist
Tanzania eyes vaccine self-sufficiency by 2030
stories.summary: Tanzania intends to produce all its vaccines locally by 2030. The goal is set a decade ahead of the African Union target, which aims for African nations to manufacture at least 60 percent of their own supply. The country has five years to bridge the gap.

stories.title: Wisconsin measles cases surpass 800
stories.summary: Wisconsin health officials reported over 130 new measles cases on November 20, bringing the annual total to 832. The outbreak has reached one-third of the state's counties, resulting in 19 hospitalizations and two deaths. The state has now exceeded its 1990 outbreak figures.

stories.title: South Korea reports first cholera case in a decade
stories.summary: South Korean health authorities confirmed a cholera case in a patient who visited a Changwon emergency room. The individual, who had not traveled overseas recently, has recovered and been discharged. Officials are currently attempting to trace the source of the infection and identify potential contacts.

stories.title: Ebola vaccine trials to begin in DR Congo
stories.summary: The World Health Organisation announced that trials for two vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo Ebola strain will begin next week. The current outbreak has resulted in 5,568 deaths out of 11,376 confirmed cases. There are currently no approved vaccines or treatments for this specific strain.

stories.title: Alcohol and eating disorders often overlap
stories.summary: Some individuals skip meals to amplify alcohol effects or save calories, a practice sometimes called drunkorexia. The behavior highlights a common crossover between risky drinking and disordered eating. The trend suggests that alcohol consumption is being used as a substitute for nutrition.

stories.title: Uzbekistan health ministry reports prevented financial violations
stories.summary: Uzbekistan's Ministry of Health reported that audits prevented 560 billion soums in violations and identified 26 billion soums in misused funds. The ministry has appointed chief compliance officers for the first time across its regional departments and has begun digitizing its land and real estate assets.

stories.title: United States loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: The United States has lost its measles elimination status after nearly three decades. The Pan American Health Organization revoked the designation following sustained domestic transmission. The status was first achieved in 2000, marking a return of a disease once considered under control.

stories.title: Measles surges as nations lose elimination status
stories.summary: The United States, Mexico, and Bolivia have lost their measles-free status amid falling vaccination rates. Health officials warn that the virus is returning to nations that previously had the infection under control. Infants are increasingly vulnerable to complications including pneumonia and respiratory failure.

stories.title: EkaCare AI scribe selected for Indian public hospitals
stories.summary: The National Health Authority has partnered with EkaCare to deploy AI voice scribes in public hospitals. The system supports over 15 Indian languages and generates clinical notes from consultations. Doctors are required to review and approve all AI-generated documentation before it enters patient records.

stories.title: India health pavilion reports thousands of visitors
stories.summary: India's Health Ministry reported 12,189 visits to its trade fair pavilion between November 14 and 18. The ministry did not disclose how many attendees received the offered AI-enabled tuberculosis screenings or provide a schedule for the daily demonstrations. The fair concludes on November 27.

stories.title: Suki OS launches to automate healthcare workflows
stories.summary: Suki has launched an agentic operating system designed to connect fragmented healthcare technology and automate administrative tasks. The platform includes a performance guarantee and aims to reduce clinical workloads through AI agents. The company plans to expand the system's capabilities beyond its existing clinician platform.

stories.title: AIIMS expands voice-based prescription pilot
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi and other medical services are expanding the use of the government's BHASHINI platform for clinical documentation. The technology supports voice-based prescriptions and multilingual communication. The rollout follows a pilot program demonstrated at the Global Digital Health Summit in New Delhi.

stories.title: BHASHINI presents multilingual AI for healthcare
stories.summary: The Digital India BHASHINI Division presented its multilingual AI ecosystem at the Global Digital Health Summit 2026. The division demonstrated how language technologies can streamline clinical workflows and improve patient-centric care. The platform is intended to promote accessible and inclusive healthcare experiences across India.

BHASHINI concludes participation at digital health summit
stories.summary: The Digital India BHASHINI Division concluded its participation at the Global Digital Health Summit 2026 in New Delhi. The division showcased its multilingual AI ecosystem, emphasizing its role in strengthening healthcare delivery and clinical workflows. The summit focused on the integration of language technology into hospital systems.

stories.title: National Dental Commission mandates registry enrollment
stories.summary: The National Dental Commission has directed all dental professionals and facilities to register under the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission. The advisory requires registration on the Healthcare Professionals Registry and the Health Facility Registry. State officials and dental colleges have been instructed to facilitate the process.

stories.title: August AI raises $12 million for patient navigation
stories.summary: August AI has raised $12 million from Accel and Peak XV Partners to deploy AI agents that manage healthcare tasks. The startup's software makes phone calls to doctors and insurers on behalf of patients. The founder stated the funds will address the difficulties of navigating the American system.

stories.title: Adult substance use at home linked to adolescent habits
stories.summary: Researchers from the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia found that adolescents living with adults who use tobacco or e-cigarettes are more likely to use substances themselves. Rates were highest when multiple adults in the home used these products. The findings were published in the journal Pediatrics.

stories.title: Daily cannabis use overtakes daily drinking for Canadians under 50
stories.summary: Six years after legalization, more adults under 50 in Canada report daily cannabis use than daily alcohol consumption. Daily cannabis smoking is now as common as daily cigarette smoking for those under 35, according to research published in the Canadian Medical Association Journal.

stories.title: UK study tracks adolescent mental health trends
stories.summary: A study published in the European Journal of Epidemiology examined psychological wellbeing and behavioral patterns among 16,000 UK adolescents aged 10 to 15 years. The research tracked changes in lifestyle and mental health between January 2009 and December 2024 to identify shifts in adolescent experiences.

stories.title: Australian MPs report mental health struggles
stories.summary: A study of Australian parliamentarians found that 7 in 10 feel their work has damaged their mental health. Nearly 40 percent of those affected say poor wellbeing has stopped them from speaking out on important issues. The findings are scheduled for release at Parliament House.

stories.title: Peer support linked to hope and social inclusion
stories.summary: The international UPSIDES trial found that structured peer support influences mental health recovery by fostering hope and social inclusion. While the intervention did not show direct effects on clinician-rated health, researchers suggest it works by cultivating psychological resources. The study provides support for this theoretical framework.

stories.title: Junk food consumption linked to lower cognitive performance
stories.summary: A study led by Flinders University found that high consumption of energy-dense, nutrient-poor foods and sugary drinks is associated with poorer mental health and cognitive performance in children and adolescents. Researchers suggest promoting healthy eating habits from an early age to support academic performance and wellbeing.

stories.title: International study links shouting to child behavioral issues
stories.summary: A study of 865 children across 14 countries found that frequently shouting at young children is linked to higher rates of behavioral and emotional problems. The research, published in Child Psychiatry and Human Development, suggests this method has a stronger association with difficulties than other disciplinary approaches.

stories.title: South African youth face financial cliff at 18
stories.summary: South Africa’s child support grant provides for 13 million children but ends at age 18. With youth unemployment exceeding 50 percent for those aged 15 to 24, researchers note that the withdrawal of support creates severe mental health impacts for young people lacking financial independence.

stories.title: Community activities linked to improved mental wellbeing
stories.summary: A study from Glasgow Caledonian University found that participating in community schemes like walking groups and gardening can boost health-related quality of life. The research, funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research, focused on the benefits of activity hubs in disadvantaged areas.

research.title: A 194-year-old tortoise has a remarkable anti-aging secret hidden in its DNA
research.summary: At an astonishing 194 years old, Jonathan the giant tortoise is the world's oldest living land animal, and scientists may have finally uncovered the secrets behind his extraordinary lifespan. Researchers identified 287 unique genetic variants linked to processes that help repair damaged DNA, control inflammation, regulate insulin, and.

research.title: A common blood pressure drug has a surprising effect on calorie-burning brown fat
research.summary: Scientists have discovered that a common blood pressure drug can activate calorie-burning brown fat in mice, potentially opening a new path toward improving metabolic health. An analysis of more than 100,000 patients also revealed surprising links between brown fat and lower rates of heart disease, diabetes, anxiety, and.

research.title: AI uncovers hidden bladder cancer warning signs years before diagnosis
research.summary: Scientists have developed an AI tool that can uncover hidden warning signs of bladder cancer up to five years before diagnosis, identifying 85% of cases in a major study involving nearly 70,000 patients. By revealing subtle patterns that conventional screening misses, the technology could help doctors detect cancer.

research.title: Alzheimer’s breakthrough exposes a hidden flaw in the brain’s cleanup system
research.summary: Scientists have identified a gene that helps the brain’s immune cells contain harmful plaques linked to Alzheimer’s, potentially revealing a new way to fight the disease. When the gene malfunctioned in mice, toxic buildup accelerated and cognitive abilities declined, raising hopes that restoring its function could help protect.

research.title: Common medications may secretly rewire your gut, with effects lasting for years
research.summary: Medications taken years or even long ago may leave lasting changes in your gut microbiome, according to a study of more than 2,500 people. Researchers discovered that common drugs, including antidepressants, blood pressure medications, and anxiety treatments, can leave microbial “fingerprints” long after patients stop taking them. Surprisingly.

research.title: Scientists discover a hidden eye disease that slowly steals night vision
research.summary: Scientists have discovered a new genetic eye disease that can silently damage peripheral and night vision while leaving central sight largely unaffected for years. The condition may be detectable through an unusual difficulty adjusting to darkness, offering a potential early warning sign before irreversible retinal damage occurs.

research.title: Type 2 diabetes linked to 53% higher Alzheimer’s risk, major review finds
research.summary: People with type 2 diabetes face a 53% higher risk of developing Alzheimer’s disease, according to a major new review of 40 studies. Researchers estimate that nearly five out of every 1,000 people with type 2 diabetes develop Alzheimer’s each year. By focusing specifically on these two conditions.
